Part 1 · Objectives and degrees of freedom

What must the control system hold, and how many handles does R-601 have?

Part 1 · the plan

From objectives to handles

  1. Control objectivesranked from safety to energy; the methanol yield is a result, not a loop
  2. The feedback loopCV, SP, MV and DV on one band-heater zone
  3. Variables classifiedwhat is controlled, moved, imposed or only watched
  4. Degrees of freedom32 variables − 21 equations = 11 handles, and who uses each
  5. Spending a DOFwhat loops, cascade, ratio, manual and saturation do to the count

Part 1 · objectives

Six objectives, in order of priority

Safety and equipment come before chemistry: no loop holds the yield; it follows from the flows and the wall temperatures.

Part 1 · the feedback loop

One loop: the E2 band-heater zone

The wall thermocouple closes the loop; the bed is outside it, so TIC-612 holds the wall, not the catalyst.

Part 1 · the feedback loop

Action and fail position are separate choices

Action

Reverse on every PID here: PV up, OUT down.

Fail position

Without signal or air: XV-601 closed, XV-401 open, heaters off.

Action is set by the process sign; fail position by the safe state.

Part 1 · variables classified

Every variable has one role

Most bed temperatures, pressures and the analyser are only watched: the loops close on flows, wall and element temperatures.

Part 1 · degrees of freedom

Counting the handlesstep 1 of 2

Objectives say what to hold. The DOF count says how many variables can be held at once.

$N_v$
steady-state variables of the unit (flows, temperatures, pressures, levels, handles)
count
$N_e$
independent equations linking them (balances, valve and pump laws)
count
$N_d,\ N_m$
disturbances fixed by the surroundings · manipulated variables
count
$$N_{DOF}=N_v-N_e=N_d+N_m\ \ \Rightarrow\ \ N_{DOF}=N_m\ \text{(disturbances given)}$$

Too many CVs and loops fight; too few and the free variables drift.

Part 1 · degrees of freedom

32 variables, 21 equationsstep 2 of 2

Previous slide$N_{DOF}=N_v-N_e$
$N_v$$N_e$$N_{DOF}$

Eleven DOF = eleven independent handles on the P&ID: three MFC valves, the pump speed, four heater powers, the BPV spring and two drain valves.

Part 1 · spending the DOF

Give each handle its user

All eleven handles are taken, so nothing is left to hold the yield directly; TIC-604 and FY-100 borrow handles that other loops own.

Part 1 · spending the DOF

What each choice does to the count

Cascade and ratio add no handle; a saturated or shared element quietly loses one.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • Objectives rank safety, equipment, quality, throughput, efficiency, energy.
  • A loop holds its CV; here the wall, not the bed.
  • R-601 has 11 DOF, all spent on flows, heaters, pressure and levels.
  • Cascade and ratio borrow handles; saturation loses them.

Part 2 · Pairing and loop structures

Which measurement goes with which handle, and in what structure?

Part 2 · the plan

Pairing first, structure second

  1. Pairing testsdirect, fast and of one sign, judged from the step tests
  2. Cascadethe wall loop inside a bed-temperature loop
  3. Ratio FY-100CO₂ and ethanol follow the measured H₂
  4. On/off and self-actingD-601 level by XV-601; pressure by BPV-601
  5. The structures on this unitwhich one, where, and why

Part 2 · pairing

What a step test tells youstep 1 of 2

Each CV needs one handle. A step in OUT, loop in MAN, shows which handle acts best.

$K$
process gain: change in PV per % change in OUT (or in % of span per %)
°C/%
$\tau$
time constant: how slowly PV moves once it starts
s
$\theta$
dead time: delay before PV starts to move
s

Good pairing: large $K$ of constant sign, small $\theta$, small $\tau$.

Part 2 · pairing

Wall or bed: which TC goes with the heater?step 2 of 2

Each band heater moves its wall TC 5 to 23 times more than the bed TC, with no dead time: the wall is the pairing.

Part 2 · pairing

Which handle sets the top of the bed?

TT-603 via E-601 elementTT-603 via E1 wall

Linear in the step tests: +5 °C on each set point, design point.

The wet top takes little heat through the wall: TT-603 is set by the preheat, so E1 is not paired with it.

Part 2 · cascade

Close the wall loop firststep 1 of 3

TT-604 t63dead time θ

Through the closed wall loop the bed answers in about half the time: the inner loop speeds up what the master sees.

Part 2 · cascade

Cascade against a single bed loopstep 2 of 3

Both bed loops remove the offset the wall loop leaves; cascade wins most when the upset hits the wall itself.

Part 2 · cascade

Why TIC-604 is normally in MANstep 3 of 3

  • The bed runs about 4 °C below the 152.5 °C dew point.
  • A master that lifts the E2 wall to chase TT-604 can dry the bed and stop the wetted ester route.
  • TT-604 carries no alarm.

In MAN the master tracks the E2 set point, so CAS starts bumpless.

Part 2 · ratio FY-100

Two ratios replace two set pointsstep 2 of 3

Previous slide$SP_{101}=F_H/r_{HC}$

At 32.7 NL/min and 5 : 4 the station returns 6.54 NL/min and 68.2 mL/min, the design set points; throughput is then one knob.

Part 2 · ratio FY-100

H₂ +15 %: ratio off or onstep 3 of 3

H₂ : CO₂ at 2 minEtOH : CO₂ at 2 min

With FY-100 off a throughput change moves the feed ratio; on, CO₂ and ethanol follow within seconds and 5 : 1 : 4 holds.

Part 2 · on/off level

D-601: level between two pointsstep 1 of 2

LT-601XV-601LT-602PT-608

XV-601 opens at 50 % and shuts at 40 %; PT-608 never moves, because liquid leaves below the gas and BPV-601 holds the pressure.

Part 2 · on/off level

The gap sets how often XV-601 cyclesstep 2 of 2

cycle periodXV-601 open foropenings per day

A wide gap means few valve strokes and big slugs to D-602; on/off suits an SOV and a level that only has to stay in its band.

Part 2 · structures

Twelve structures, and where R-601 uses them

Single PI loops do most of the work; cascade, ratio, on/off and a self-acting regulator cover the rest.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Heaters pair with wall TCs; the preheat sets the top of the bed.
  • Cascade TIC-604 → TIC-612 is available but normally in MAN.
  • FY-100 holds 5 : 1 : 4 through a throughput change.
  • D-601 cycles every 75 min on/off; BPV-601 holds the pressure.

Part 3 · P, PI, PID and tuning

How do P, I and D act, and how are the loops tuned from step tests?

Part 3 · the plan

From the PID routine to a tuning

  1. The PID routinewhat every faceplate computes every 0.25 s
  2. P and IP leaves an offset; I removes it, but too fast it overshoots
  3. FOPDT from a step test$K$, $\tau$ and $\theta$ from two points of the curve
  4. Lambda tuningone knob, the closed-loop speed, against the simulator's own tuning
  5. Reading a closed-loop traceovershoot, settling, offset and IAE

Part 3 · the PID routine

One routine on every faceplate

$e$
error SP% − PV%, both in % of the transmitter span (reverse acting)
%
$K_c$
controller gain: % OUT per % error
–
$T_i,\ T_d$
integral (reset) time, derivative time; $T_i$ = 0 switches I off
s
$$OUT=K_c\,e+\dfrac{K_c}{T_i}\int e\,dt-K_c\,T_d\,\dfrac{dPV}{dt}$$

D acts on PV, not on $e$; OUT clamped 0–100 % with anti-windup.

Part 3 · P and I

Why P alone leaves an offsetstep 1 of 2

PID routine, I and D off$OUT=OUT_0+K_c\,e$
$\Delta PV=K\,\Delta OUT-d$steady process: gain $K$, load $d$ in % of span
$e=-\Delta PV,\quad \Delta OUT=K_c\,e$SP fixed; P term is the only change
$e=\dfrac{d}{1+K_c\,K}$substitute and solve for the error

Offset shrinks with $K_c$ but never reaches zero; I is needed.

Part 3 · P and I

TIC-612 on P only: ethanol −15 %step 2 of 2

Previous slide$e=\dfrac{d}{1+K_c\,K}$
offset, formulaoffset, model run

The model's P-only runs fall on the formula; PI at the same Kc ends with zero offset.

Part 3 · P and I

Integral time on TIC-612: SP +5 °C

overshootsettles (±0.5 °C)IAE

With $K_c$ 3, a $T_i$ far below the wall's 8 min time constant buys overshoot, not speed; $T_i$ = τ gives none.

Part 3 · FOPDT

Fitting a step teststep 1 of 2

Tuning by trial is slow on an 8-minute wall. A step test gives a model to tune on.

Pairing symbols$K$ gain · $\tau$ time constant · $\theta$ dead time
$y,\ y_0$
PV after and before the step
eng.
$\Delta u$
OUT step in MAN
%
$y(t)=y_0+K\,\Delta u\left(1-e^{-(t-\theta)/\tau}\right),\ t>\theta$first order plus dead time response
$t_{28}=\theta+\tau/3,\quad t_{63}=\theta+\tau$set $y$ to 28.3 % and 63.2 % of the change
$\tau=1.5\,(t_{63}-t_{28}),\quad \theta=t_{63}-\tau$subtract the two times; Smith's two-point method

Part 3 · FOPDT

The step tests of R-601, fittedstep 2 of 2

Previous slide$\tau=1.5\,(t_{63}-t_{28})$
$K$, %/%$\tau$$\theta$

Flows answer in about a second, walls in 8–10 min; only the bed TCs and the cascade master carry real dead time.

Part 3 · lambda tuning

One knob: the closed-loop speedstep 1 of 3

$\lambda$
chosen closed-loop time constant (lambda, the IMC tuning rule)
s
FOPDT fit$K,\ \tau,\ \theta$ from the step test
$$K_c=\dfrac{\tau}{K\,(\lambda+\theta)},\qquad T_i=\tau$$

$\lambda=\tau$: calm, no overshoot. $\lambda=\tau/3$: tight. Larger $\lambda$ is more robust.

Part 3 · lambda tuning

Lambda tuning labstep 2 of 3

Lambda rule$K_c=\tau/[K(\lambda+\theta)]$
$K_c$ · $T_i$overshoot (FOPDT)overshoot (model)

λ trades speed for overshoot. The FOPDT forecast holds on the walls but misses TIC-604's overshoot: check a tuning on the model.

Part 3 · lambda tuning

The simulator's tuning, judgedstep 3 of 3

Times from model runs at the design point; settling bands ±0.5 °C, ±0.2 °C for TT-604.

Part 3 · reading a trace

Scrub a closed-loop test

PV · SPOUTresult

Watch OUT, not only PV: the handle moves first, and a PV back on SP with OUT still drifting is not settled.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • P leaves $e=d/(1+K_cK)$; I removes it.
  • $T_i$ far below τ overshoots without settling faster.
  • A step test gives $K$, τ, θ; lambda gives $K_c$ and $T_i$.
  • The simulator's wall loops overshoot; TIC-604's $T_i$ is too slow.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Count the DOF before drawing loops: R-601 has eleven handles.

2

Pair each CV with a direct, fast handle of one sign.

3

Close the wall loop first; cascade the bed onto it only with care.

4

Ratio the feeds to the measured H₂ when throughput moves.

5

Tune from a step test: FOPDT, then lambda, then check the trace.
